prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1065; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle struck the rear of claimant vehicle while stopped at a red light. Police report requested. Insured reports sudden braking by the other driver but acknowledges following distance was too short. Liability preliminarily assessed as predominantly insured.

Entry 2: Claimant reports neck and wrist pain at scene and was transported to urgent care. Claimant has since retained counsel, who has requested that all further communication be routed through their office. Letter of representation received and logged. Direct contact with claimant suspended.

Entry 3: Medical records received from treating provider. Diagnosis confirmed as a fracture of the distal radius of the left wrist, treated with casting and a follow-up orthopedic consult. Treating physician notes possible physical therapy referral. Records reviewed and forwarded to the medical review unit for causation confirmation.

Entry 4: Counsel's demand package received, including itemized medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a narrative of ongoing symptoms. Demand is under review. Requested clarification from counsel regarding the scope of the physical therapy claimed and whether any prior wrist complaints exist. Response deadline noted in the file.

Entry 5: Independent medical examination scheduled through counsel's office, with claimant's consent. Reserve adjusted to reflect injury severity and anticipated treatment duration. Supervisor notified of litigation risk given representation and fracture diagnosis. File flagged for senior adjuster review before any settlement discussion.
